description.value:
The six discrete Morrell tongue label parts comprise three labels for canned tongue (see below). They share certain design elements: a navy blue background; large, white serif-style type for the product name; smaller gilt upper case type for details of the package contents; and images of plated sliced tongue, photographed in color. Some details vary: in the ox tongue version, the garnish is parsley, and unseen hands hold a knife in the act of slicing the tongue, thus adding to the already plated contents; in the lunch tongue version, a dark green leaf is accompanied by two radishes.

1956-47-84-cc and 1956-47-84-ff comprise one label, imprinted Morrell/ ox/ tongue.
1956-47-84-aa and 1956-47-84-ee comprise one label, imprinted Morrell/ lunch/ tongue.
1956-47-84-bb and 1956-47-84-dd comprise one label, imprinted Morrell/ lunch/ tongue.

Album, pages 4 and 5.

summary.title: Drawings, Prints, and Graphic Design Department

description.value:
The six heads of Roman rulers, scattered on the page, are labeled in script. On the top left of the page, the head, almost bald and in frontal view, is turned slightly to the left; the eyes, looking in that direction, are wide open; the visible (left) brow is raised, while the brow area on the right is heavily shaded; the jaw, also shaded, is square. The label, Scipio/ Africanus, is underneath.

Next, to the right, just off center, is a head posed on a long neck, in right profile. Hair is indicated by a few wavy lines on the back of the head; the nose is aquiline, the face heavily shadowed, and the chin receding. The label, Claudius Marcellus, is on the right; from old coin, just underneath, alludes to a stylistic source. 

On the far right, the lightly sketched head is in right profile; the aquiline nose, full lower lip, and cleft chin are the distinctive features. Mitridates/ the great is written on the right just next to the edge of the page.

In the space underneath the Claudius label is a head in right profile; the darker outline and shading of forehead, nose and mouth emphasize those features. The label, Perseus, is on the right. With the sheet turned top to bottom, the head on the left in right profile shows an upturned nose and rounded chin; dark outlines and heavy shading prevail. Pompeiius is the label underneath. 

On the same level to the right, the head, turned toward the left, features deep horizontal creases in the forehead and heavy shading throughout. The right eyebrow curves vertically into the space between the eyes. A curly fringe indicates the hairline. Sulla, written on the right, is followed by the designer's parenthetical notation: more mean looking - eyes closed - squinting.

legal.credit: Gift of Ellen Gustav Jensen

description.value:
The present black and white photograph displays a round jar with a screw-on lid. The lid design features three small spirals placed at the center as if marking the points of a triangle; between the spirals, Bennetts, etched horizontally, radiates three times to the rim. A label affixed to the jar is imprinted Silver/ Bennetts/ Polish, with silver and polish in the designer's hand-lettered style type, in silver on black, and Bennetts in smaller stencil-style type in black on silver; spiral designs flank silver and polish on the left and right. Two lines of instructions regarding use of the product are imprinted in small sans-serif capitals in black on silver on the bottom row of the label. 

The silver-and-black color scheme has been confirmed by an actual label present in the Gustav Jensen inventory.

description.value: The present object, here stored flat, is a label designed to encircle a can of luncheon meat. All type is imprinted in white on a pale purple background. Below a narrow strip at the top, imprinted with the manufacturer's name, Arbogast & Bastian Inc, is A Suggestion for Serving, heading each of two side by side identical photographs of a platter comprised of four sausages on a bed of a green leafy vegetable garnished with four radishes. A & B, in block serif-style, is superimposed on the photograph at the center. In the lower half, the label continues: Old Fashioned [antique type]/ Country Style [serif style]/ Pork Sausages [serif-style, bold], followed by three lines of additional product information. Between the photographs, perpendicular to the horizontal type, are five lines of type headed Serving Suggestions.

description.value: The present object, here stored flat, is a label designed to wrap a rectangular can with rounded corners. The type is white throughout and the background, except for the product photograph, is pale purple. Below a narrow strip at the top imprinted with the manufacturer's name, Arbogast & Bastian Inc., are two side by side identical color photographs, each featuring a platter covered with sliced meat garnished with sprigs of a dark green leafy vegetable. Just below the top edge of the photograph, A Suggestion For Serving is imprinted; the product logo, A & B, in serif-style block letters, is superimposed on the meat at the center. A wide light band stretching across below the photograph is imprinted Luncheon/ Meat in serif-style type; additional type provides product details. Perpendicular to and between the photographs are six lines of type headed Serving Suggestions. A decorative rick rack pattern in light purple and gray is located where the two halves of the label meet when positioned on the can.

legal.credit: Gift of Ellen Gustav Jensen
